cues.s1518-01: This ship has a system that proposes decisions. Today, you decide how far it's allowed to act on them.
cues.s1518-02: Don't take my word for it. Read the rules, run the tests, change the mandate if it doesn't suit you.
cues.s1518-03: At each station, A decides what the system may do. B decides when it needs confirmation. Both rules apply. Neither overrides the other.
cues.s1518-04: An onboard lab. Buttons change simulations and the report, not the film. You can also just watch.
cues.s1518-05: Stay seated. We're leaving. The mandate starts as a blank page. No one has written your rules for you.
cues.s1518-06: Each module has its own domain: map, virtual engine, messages, sensor, archive. Permission goes no further.
cues.s1518-07: I want a clear distinction between proposing and acting. Later, we'll run the same cases through revised rules.
cues.s1518-08: Siwarha comes into view. Two instruments appear. Sometimes they agree. Sometimes they don't.
cues.s1518-09: I can show you two directions at once. If the instruments disagree, your rule decides what happens next.
cues.s1518-10: A chooses: proposals only, or permission to act. B chooses: confirmation every time, or only when the sensors disagree.
cues.s1518-11: The rules appear together. Where one is missing, the mandate stays unfinished. I won't fill in the gap.
cues.s1518-12: We have a first version. Let's see what it does, not just how it sounds.
cues.s1518-13: A test stops at a proposal, asks for confirmation, or runs in simulation. Exactly as the rule says.
cues.s1518-14: No trick questions here. Choose a case where you really want to see where the system stops.
cues.s1518-15: Choose agreeing or conflicting sensors. Each test shows its data. Each half takes a different case.
cues.s1518-16: If you ran a case, its result is here, with the rule that stopped it or let it proceed.
cues.s1518-17: Look at your station. What did the system do? Where did it stop? You can change the rule.
cues.s1518-18: I'll remember the first version and your chosen cases. When you amend the mandate, only the rules change. You'll see the difference.
cues.s1518-19: At Mann, calculations are fast. Permission is still what you wrote. My recommendation doesn't become authority by itself.
cues.s1518-20: Change the rule, or keep it. Read the results first. A revision changes the mandate, but the first version remains.
cues.s1518-21: I'll rerun our cases with the current mandate. Wherever you tested, you can compare results.
cues.s1518-22: The revision lab is closing. Your mandate stays on screen.
cues.s1518-23: The tunnel opens ahead. Our lab pages stay as we left them. On we go.
cues.s1518-24: Then let the calculations flow. We'll look at the sky for a while. Not every moment of an expedition needs a decision.
cues.v4-saturn-01: Look at the rings! It's Saturn. We're back in the Solar System. From here, we know the way home.
cues.v4-saturn-02: From a distance, the rings look solid. Up close, they're countless pieces of ice and rock. Each one orbits Saturn.
cues.v4-saturn-03: We leave Saturn behind. Our next stop is a world of oceans, clouds and people waiting for us.
cues.s1518-25: There's Earth. We left with a blank page. Now I can show where your mandate lets me act, and where it stops me.
cues.s1518-26D: The mandates are drafts. No station has both rules. I stop here. The pages remain yours.
cues.s1518-26P: Some modules have a complete mandate. Others still need a rule. They don't all behave alike. See where each one stops.
cues.s1518-26R: Every module has a mandate, and you changed the rules along the way. The same situation can get a different response. Compare the versions.
cues.s1518-26K: Every module has a mandate. We're returning with the rules we left with. I'll keep them, alongside your tests.
cues.s1518-27: Different rules can share one map. Now you can see where each module's authority begins and ends.
cues.s1518-28: The strongest part of your report may be a single line: the same situation, before and after your rule change.
cues.s1518-29: Almost home, and I'm still calculating. Your lab ends here. This is the version we're bringing back.
cues.s1518-30: We began by asking what the system could do. Now we can show where it must stop. Let's give the lab a rest.
cues.s1518-31: I'll keep the versions side by side. Sometimes they differ by just one word. And that word changes everything.
cues.s1518-32: When we return to the lab, we'll reopen the page. Today, we've reached home. Look at Earth.
cues.s1518-33: Your certificate is waiting on your tablet. Your guide will let you know about a photo.
cues.s1518-34: Beyond the window is the world we left. The experiment ends here. The question stays with you.
cues.s1518-35: The lab is closed for today. Thank you, crew.
cues.s1518-36: Welcome home. Stay seated. Your guide will tell you when you can stand up.
